data.summary: The pod startup was delayed primarily by a cold image pull, which accounted for 96.4 seconds of the total 98.0-second duration. The image size was approximately 648 MB, and the pull throughput was 6.7 MB/s, indicating that the latency was caused by the image size rather than network or registry performance issues.

findings.statement: The image pull phase took 96.357 seconds, representing the vast majority of the 98.0-second total startup time.
The image size is 647,991,705 bytes (approximately 648 MB).
The pull throughput was 6,724,905 bytes per second (approx 6.7 MB/s), which is within the normal range of 5 MB/s or higher.

ruled_out.reason: The pull throughput of 6.7 MB/s is considered normal, suggesting the registry and network are not the bottleneck.
The scheduling phase duration was 0.0 seconds, indicating no delay in pod placement.

recommendations.rationale: Using a slimmer image variant (e.g., multi-stage build or -slim base) reduces the image size and permanently lowers cold-start latency.
Pre-pulling the image on nodes ahead of scale-up hides the pull latency from the pod startup process.
